chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If a servant performs Hajj ten times, there would still be upon him the Hajj of Islam as well, when he has the capacity to do so. And if a young boy performs Hajj ten times, then attains puberty, upon him would be the Obligation of Islam. And if an owned slave performs Hajj ten times, then is freed, upon him would be the Obligation of Islam, when he has the capacity for it.
ai.seo_question: Does performing Hajj ten times as a slave or child exempt one from the obligatory Hajj later?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that voluntary or pre-liability Hajj acts do not substitute for the obligatory Hajj al-Islam, even if performed ten times by slaves or pre-pubertal boys. It establishes a key principle in Shia jurisprudence that the 'Hajj of Islam' is a distinct, subsequent duty triggered only upon attaining full legal capacity (freedom for slaves, puberty for boys), ensuring the ritual's completeness is tied to the individual's mature status.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If a servant performs Hajj ten times, there would (still) be upon him a Hajj of Al-Islam as well, when he has the capacity to that. And if a young boy were to perform Hajj ten times, then attains puberty, upon him would be an Obligation of Al-Islam, and if an owned slave performs Hajj ten times, then is freed, upon him would be an Obligation of Al-Islam, when he has the capacity for it’.
en.sarwar: 18. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm from Misma’ ibn ‘Abd al-Malik who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Even if a servant of Allah performs ten al-Hajj, he owes obligatory Hajjahta al-Islam also; if he is able to perform Hajjahta al-Islam. If a boy performs ten al- Hajj ah, he owes obligatory Hajjahta al-Islam also; if he is able to perform Hajjahta al-Islam when he becomes an adult. If a slave performs ten al-Hajj ah, then is set free that person owes obligatory Hajjahta al-Islam also, if he is able to perform Hajjahta al-Islam.”’
